title: Hatcliffe Top Lancaster Memorial

external_narratives.summary: The IWM register lists this memorial as commemorating Lancaster JB596 of 100 Squadron. The crash occurred on 17 December 1943, part of the notorious 'Black Thursday' Berlin raid when thick fog caused heavy losses among returning crews.
key_details: Part of Black Thursday losses 16-17 December 1943
25 Lancasters lost on Berlin operation plus 31 more on return due to fog

external_narratives.summary: Photographic record of the memorial stone at Hatcliffe Top showing it incorporates a piece of the aircraft's skin and relics from the crash. The Lancaster hit a tree close to the memorial site and crashed into the pine trees behind.
key_details: Aircraft hit treetop before crashing into pine plantation

external_narratives.summary: CWGC records confirm crew details for the Black Thursday losses. The pilot Flg Off. Robert Laval Proudfoot was aged 24. Four crew were killed (Proudfoot, Sgt Sidney David Viggers aged 19, Sgt John Bamford aged 23, Sgt Bernard Heaton aged 21) while three crew survived with serious injuries. A farm worker was severely burned rescuing survivors from the blaze.

memorial_details:
Memorial in the form of a grave with rectangular stone of Remembrance at head and kerb stones bordering the area. Two dedicatory plaques placed on the stone and one at the foot of the kerbstones. Names of the dead marked with a cross and the injured with an asterisk. Coloure Crest of 100 Squadron at top and silhouette of a Lancaster Bomber at centre.

Memorial Unveiling: The unveiling of the Avro Lancaster JB596 memorial.
narrative:
On the night of 17 December 1943, Lancaster JB596 (coded HW-H) of 100 Squadron, based at RAF Grimsby, was returning from a raid on Berlin. The aircraft clipped a treetop and crashed into pine trees at Hatcliffe Top. The crash was part of the losses associated with 'Black Thursday', when thick fog over Lincolnshire caused heavy casualties among returning crews: 25 Lancasters were lost on the Berlin operation and 31 more were lost or damaged on return due to fog. Three crew survived with serious injuries; four were killed, including pilot Flg Off Robert Laval Proudfoot, aged 24. A local farm worker was severely burned while attempting to rescue survivors from the blaze.

A local farm worker was severely burned attempting to rescue survivors from the burning wreck, a personal cost that the crash imposed directly on the Hatcliffe community.
inscription:
PLAQUE ONE: REMEMBERING THE CREW OF AVRO LANCASTER MKIII
JB 596 HW - H - 100 SQDN
CRASHED ON THIS SITE
DEC 17TH 1943 ON RETURN
FROM BERLIN
[crew names inscribed on memorial] PLAQUE TWO: NOW HARVESTS OF GOLD CORN HERE ARE GATHERED
NO SWORDS NOW BUT PLOUGHSHARES INSTEAD
AND THE TREES OF PINE STAND SENTINAL (SIC)
OVER THE FIELD WHER LIFESBLOOD WAS SHED
KATHYRYN REID A.L.A.M. (HONS)
 PLAQUE THREE: PRAY PAUSE BY THIS MEMORIAL
AND BEFORE YOU GO
REMEMBER
THE DEBT TO BRAVE BOMBER COMMAND AIRMENT
WE WILL FOREVER OWE
KR & RS
community_connection: The memorial, which names both the dead and the injured with distinct markings, records the full human toll of the crash including those who survived with serious injuries.
